live_gaps.cause: No code failure and no error: the monthly runbook was simply never invoked. Attention went to the Markov diagnostics (2026-07-30 → 2026-08-19, layer shelved) and the news-backfill fix (2026-08-11). The 2026-07-13 run was the last live invocation.
live_gaps.cause_amendment_2026-09-01: The 'no code failure' characterisation is incomplete. A latent bug in feature_matrix._load_fundamental_scores() built its monthly forward-fill scaffold ending at the last QUARTER-end rather than the requested month-end, so months after the last completed quarter came back with 13/20 factor columns NaN (65% > the 50% NAN_DROP_THRESHOLD) and were dropped entirely. The feature matrix could therefore only ever reach the last completed quarter. Sprint 8 did not surface this because 2026-06-30 IS a quarter-end. Had the 2026-08-03 rebalance been invoked on schedule it would have scored 2026-06 and silently rebalanced into a stale month. Fixed 2026-09-01 by extending the scaffold to max(last_quarter_end, requested_end); the change is purely additive (+106 rows = 2 months x 53 tickers, no historical row altered) and restores the behaviour the function's docstring already specified. No model, FEATURE_COLS, MIN_SCORE, TOP_N or pickle change.

exit_defect.summary: Fractional positions cannot be fully exited by paper_runner. Both the primary and fallback order paths under-sell.
exit_defect.mechanism_1_notional_rejection: The primary path submits a notional sell equal to the position's market value at query time. Any adverse move between query and submission makes that notional exceed the live position value, and Alpaca rejects it (code 40310000).
exit_defect.mechanism_2_retry_truncates_and_uses_sta: broker_alpaca._submit_one falls back to qty = max(1, int(notional / _latest_price(t))). _latest_price reads the most recent adj_close from the prices table, which on 2026-09-02 was the 2026-08-31 close - one session stale and, that day, HIGHER than the live price for all five names. Both errors under-sell: int() truncates the fraction, and the stale-high price buys fewer shares per dollar of notional.
exit_defect.mechanism_verified: int(target_notional / 2026-08-31 adj_close) reproduces all five realised fills exactly: ACLS int(15326.40/115.33)=132; FORM int(16740.11/100.61)=166; MRVL int(18088.83/211.66)=85; ON int(15510.17/74.09)=209; QCOM int(17787.30/170.48)=104. Confirmed, not inferred.

breadth_rules.decided_blind: Fixed in advance of knowing which ticker it would ever apply to. At the time of decision no n<=1 month had occurred on the live book; the live book stood at n=2 (AMAT, HPE) for 2026-08 and this rule is an exact no-op on that book. The point of pre-committing was to remove discretion from a future month whose affected name is unknowable today.
breadth_rules.rule_name: bound the unobserved tail; cap tighter than observed behaviour
breadth_rules.cap_rationale: 0.60 is the n=2 x RISK_ON weight (1.2/2). The cap is TIGHTER THAN OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR - the maximum per-name weight ever observed is 1.00, from two profitable n=1 x NEUTRAL months (2024-01 FTNT, 2024-03 DELL). The rule therefore accepts a measured -0.036 Sharpe / -5.6pp test-fold cost, incurred precisely by clipping those two profitable months, in exchange for bounding the UNOBSERVED n=1 x RISK_ON case at 120%. This is a real constraint with a real cost, not a formalization of existing behaviour.

behaviour.n_eq_0: All cash. scaled_weight = 0.0. UNCHANGED from existing behaviour.
behaviour.n_eq_1: per_name_weight = min(multiplier/1, 0.60); remainder to cash. Binds at NEUTRAL (1.0 -> 0.60) and RISK_ON (1.2 -> 0.60). Does NOT bind at RISK_OFF (0.5 -> 0.5), which is intended: 50% is already below the 0.60 cap.
behaviour.n_ge_2: per_name_weight = min(multiplier/n, 0.60). UNCHANGED in every observed case: the cap is inactive for all n>=2 at every multiplier, and at n=2 x RISK_ON it returns exactly 0.60, bit-identical to the uncapped value.

implementation_spec.form: min(weight, 0.60) applied to the post-multiplier per-name weight.
implementation_spec.required_test: Assert the n=2 x RISK_ON per-name weight is BIT-IDENTICAL before and after, comparing against the UNCAPPED COMPUTATION - min(RISK_ON_MULT/2, CAP) == RISK_ON_MULT/2 - not against the literal 0.60. On CPython 1.2/2 and 0.60 happen to round to the same double (0x1.3333333333333p-1), so a literal assertion would pass today, but it would be passing by coincidence and would break silently if RISK_ON_MULT or the cap were ever retuned. The uncapped-computation form tests the invariant that actually matters: that the cap does not perturb the n=2 book.
implementation_spec.deadline: MUST land before the October rebalance (2026-10-01). rebalance.py:146 (scaled_weight = regime_multiplier / n_selected) and the equivalent line in portfolio_builder.py (1.0 / n_selected) are both still UNBOUNDED. Breadth was 2 in 2026-08, so n=1 is plausibly the next month, not a distant tail.

evidence.method: Expanding-window out-of-sample: each month scored by its own fold (78 folds, 2018-06 -> 2024-11, 4-month purge); holdout scored by folds[-1] as src/live/scorer.py does. Holdout reconstruction reproduces the vintage's holdout_scores.parquet bit-identically (max|diff| = 0.0, n=954).
evidence.coverage_limitation: Folds begin 2018-06-30, so no OOS scores exist for 2015-03 -> 2018-05; roughly 40% of the nominal Sprint 5 training window is unmeasurable by this method.
evidence.n1_impact_on_test_fold: Both n=1 months were profitable. Holding them: Sharpe 0.822, maxDD -24.87%, total +35.76%. Sending them to cash: Sharpe 0.631, maxDD -24.87%, total +21.13% (-0.191 Sharpe, -14.63pp, zero drawdown relief). n=1 is therefore ALREADY inside the 2023-24 test-fold result the project relies on.
evidence.cap_binding_frequency: 2 of 88 months (2.3%) - only the two n=1 months. Exact no-op on the holdout and on every n>=2 month.
evidence.note_120pct_never_observed: n=1 has never co-occurred with RISK_ON in 88 months. Both n=1 months were NEUTRAL, so the observed exposure was 100%, not the 120% worst case.
evidence.correction_to_sprint7: sprint7_results.json records breadth_min_2025_26 = 2, but on the frozen vintage the holdout minimum is 3 (mean 15.22 vs 14.89; median 14 and max 53 match). The n=2 months in this reconstruction are 2023-12-31 and 2024-06-30, both in the TEST FOLD, not the holdout. The claim that a two-name month sits inside the Sharpe-1.016 holdout does not reproduce on this vintage - most likely AV backfill revisions between the Sprint 7 run and the 2026-08-04 freeze.
evidence.reconstruction_caveat: Reconstructed test Sharpe 0.822 vs Sprint 7 published 0.990, and holdout 1.356 vs 1.016; this is a simplified rebuild, not the full backtest pipeline. Figures are internally consistent RELATIVE comparisons, not restatements.
evidence.post_hoc_disclosure: Options B and C were specified AFTER observing that both historical n=1 months were profitable. The chosen cap is therefore not blind to that fact, though it is blind to any future affected ticker.

breadth_rules.correction_2026-09-02: An earlier draft of this entry claimed 0.60 was 'the maximum per-name weight ever reached in a validated backtest'. That was FALSE and contradicted this entry's own max_per_name_weight_ever_observed = 1.00. The claim, and three further sentences resting on it (the rule name, the RISK_OFF 'tested ceiling' note, and the float-literal form of the required test), were struck before this entry landed. The cap is tighter than observed behaviour and carries a measured cost; it is not a formalization of what the strategy already did.
